rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The pronoun refers implicitly to the Qur’an because its antecedent is clear from context.
rows.anchor: Since the context is clear, this pronoun occurs for something that is understood.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The verb describes revelation delivered painstakingly and thoroughly.
rows.anchor: means to reveal something painstakingly and in a thorough way.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The rejecters are warned that the Qur’an is unlike the devils’ inspiration to soothsayers and should not be denied.
rows.anchor: The rejecters and adversaries of the Qur’ ān are warned here that it has not something similar to what the soothsayers are inspired from the devils.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The Trusted Spirit is Gabriel; his title ‘trusted’ affirms that he conveyed the revelation faithfully as received.
rows.anchor: is the title of Gabriel. The attribute “trusted” shows that he has delivered it to the Prophet (sws) in a faithful way exactly as he received it.

rows.speaker: the Jews and the Raw āfiḍ
rows.claim: The Jews and Rawāfiḍ accused Gabriel of dishonesty in conveying revelation to the Prophet.
rows.anchor: the Jews and the Raw āfiḍ had blamed Gabriel of dishonesty in this matter.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The pronoun refers to Prophet Muhammad; revelation reaches his heart rather than his imagination.
rows.anchor: Prophet Mu ḥammad (sws). In other words, it is the heart and not his fancy that is the recipient of divine revelation.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The heart is the noblest human organ and cannot be invaded by satanic whisper or interference.
rows.anchor: The heart is the most noble organ of human body. Hence there is no chance that it be invaded by any satanic whisper or interference.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Although the address is to the Prophet, its purpose is to show opponents that the Qur’an comes from a pure source and descends at a pure place.
rows.anchor: the purpose is to explain to the opponents that the Qur’ān has originated from a pure source and descended at a pure place.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The revelation makes the Prophet warn people heedless of God and the Hereafter; the Qur’an warns of the consequences, so people must heed it.
rows.anchor: the purpose of Qur’ān’s revelation: the Prophet (sws) should fully make aware all those who are leading their lives while being indifferent to God and the Hereafter of the consequence of this indifference.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Eloquent Arabic is God’s favor to the Arabs, honors them, and makes the truth conclusively clear so they cannot plead that they did not understand.
rows.anchor: the Qur’ ān has been revealed in eloquent Arabic, which is a means of honour for them and is also a conclusive communication of the truth to them.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Earlier scriptures contain prophecies of the Prophet’s advent and call, known to Israelite scholars though concealed by most; some accepted the Qur’an and Muhammad.
rows.anchor: among them were the true scholars too who openly acknowledged the Qur’ ān and also professed faith in Muḥammad (sws).

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The cited prophecies and believing Israelite scholars challenge the opponents: the author asks what further proof they require.
rows.anchor: In the above cited verses, these very prophesies and these scholars are referred and the question posed to the opponents of the Qur’ ān. What more do they want.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Arabs considered the People of the Book religiously superior, yet denial blinded them: they treated supportive unbelievers as well-wishers and believers in Muhammad as conspirators.
rows.anchor: in religious issues the Arabs regarded the People of Book to be superior. However, in frenzy of their denial of the Prophet (sws), they had become so blind

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The author says his reading of the verse is clear and has parallels in earlier and later sūrahs.
rows.anchor: Its parallels can be seen in the earlier sūrahs as well as in the succeeding ones.

rows.speaker: some people
rows.claim: Some have attributed to the jurists the deduction that the Qur’an may be read in a non-Arabic language.
rows.anchor: some people have ascribed an opinion to our jurists that they have deduced from this verse

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The author rejects that deduction: a rendering into another language is a translation, not the Qur’an, and no translated verse or sūrah can replace the Arabic original.
rows.anchor: If the Qur’ ān is rendered into another language, it cannot be called the Qur’ ān; it will be its translation and there is great difference between a text and its translation.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Even with clear meanings and a capable translator, the Qur’an’s full meaning and eloquence cannot be rendered; translations of other scriptures also cannot replace their originals.
rows.anchor: after years of hard work, when he gets down to translating them, he feels that, in spite of having the ability to translate, he is not able to fully render the verses, let alone their eloquence.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: He says Jews and Christians went astray in part because original scriptural languages died out and translations became substitutes grounding their understanding and reasoning.
rows.anchor: the major reason for the Jews and Christians going astray is that the original languages of their scriptures became extinct and they regarded their translations to be their substitute.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The author says Saint Paul manipulated translations to lead Christians astray.
rows.anchor: I have already explained at an appropriate instance how Saint Paul manipulated the translations to lead the Christians astray.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: He calls the juristic deduction groundless and gravely consequential, suggesting it was attributed to the jurists through misunderstanding.
rows.anchor: I think that this deduction from the verse has no grounds and is totally wrong in itself; in fact, it is a matter of grave consequence

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Had the Qur’an been in a foreign tongue, Arabs could have claimed an excuse; since it came in their finest language to their best person, they have none.
rows.anchor: what is the excuse they have when the Qur’ ān has been revealed in their own best language to a best person among them.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The author connects this point to 41:44, where opponents object to a foreign-language Qur’an for Arab addressees, and directs readers to 16:103 for a specific aspect.
rows.anchor: The discourse in a foreign tongue, and the addressees Arabs?

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Salaka here means to make something enter something.
rows.anchor: also means “to make something enter something.” Here it is used in this meaning.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The Qur’an’s rejection reflects hearts ruined by persistent sin, not a fault in the Qur’an; its truth reaches them but their disposition refuses it, like people unable to retain good nourishment.
rows.anchor: Persistence in sin has corrupted these hearts so much that they have lost their ability to accept the truth.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: By God’s established practice, such people will recognize the Qur’an’s truth only upon seeing the sudden punishment; their later plea for respite comes too late.
rows.anchor: Now these people will accept the veracity of the Qur’ān only when they see the punishment it is informing them of.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The question expresses amazement that people demand punishment; delay does not avert it, respite follows divine wisdom, and mockery of its delay is their misfortune.
rows.anchor: Any delay in its arrival does not secure them from it. If God has granted them the respite to live and enjoy until a certain period of time, this will not make any difference.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: God’s just and merciful practice is not to destroy a nation before warning it and conclusively delivering the truth; if it rejects the reminder, its fate is exact justice.
rows.anchor: Since He is just and merciful, He does not destroy a nation without warning it and conclusively delivering the truth to it.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The term ‘reminder’ explains why messengers come, and the wording emphasizes that God never destroys a nation without such warning.
rows.anchor: expounds the reason of a messenger’s advent and the style shows that it is being emphasized that without such a reminder, God does not destroy a nation.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Refusing the reminder makes the resulting punishment just, not an injustice by God.
rows.anchor: If they do not duly value this reminder, they shall have to face the destined result and this would not be any injustice.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Verse 210 reverses the positive statement in 26:192: the Qur’an is sent by God, not by the devils as Quraysh claimed.
rows.anchor: What was stated earlier in verse 192 in a positive sense, is stated here in a negative one.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Devils are unworthy of the Qur’an and unable to bring it; doing so would oppose their mission and destroy their own kingdom.
rows.anchor: neither are they worthy of it not is it in line with their mission. How can they destroy their own kingdom by their own hands?

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The author compares the charge against the Qur’an with Pharisees’ claim that Jesus performed miracles through Beelzebul, the chief demon.
rows.anchor: they started to say the masses that it is with the help of Beelzebul, the chief evil, spirit that he shows these miracles:
